title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1966-09-16

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1966 soundboard capture of the early Dead with solid, vintage‑era audio and standout blues‑rock numbers like “I Know You Rider,” “Dancing In The Streets,” and “Midnight Hour.”
ai_review.review: The recording is a soundboard source that, while not flawless by modern standards, delivers surprisingly clear and balanced audio for a 1966 tape. Musically the show is celebrated as an early‑Dead high point – tight blues‑rock performances, soaring Pigpen vocals/harp and hot Jerry Garcia solos make it a must‑listen for any era‑spanning collection.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high 4–5 star reviews praise both the performance and the surprisingly good sound quality; weighted rating leans toward an excellent show with good (but not perfect) recording.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Sound is described as 'quite good' for a 1966 tape, crisp enough to hear Jerry up‑front; some reviewers note mix could be tighter and occasional minor flaws, but overall the audio is listenable and better than many contemporary bootlegs.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A blues‑rock heavy set that showcases the Dead as a high‑energy dance band; songs flow naturally with Pigpen’s organ/harmonica leading many numbers and Garcia weaving lead guitar around them.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly called 'hot', 'smoking' and front‑and‑center in the mix; his solos on “Dancing In The Streets” and other cuts are highlighted as exceptional.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted occasionally as sounding good, which was rare for 1966 recordings; praised for solid rhythm work on this show.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ is described as swirling and a lead instrument, creating the signature early‑Dead soundscape.
band_member_comments.Drums: Few specific comments; one reviewer mentions drums could be mixed better but overall the rhythm section drives the high‑energy feel.
